races.title: State Senate, District 34
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kevin Crutchfield
cands.bio: Small business owner in Concord, NC. Former IBM employee who co-founded Casco Signs in 1998. Republican member of the NC House (District 83) from 2023 to 2025. Won the March 2026 Republican primary for State Senate District 34.

controversies.text: In December 2024, WBTV reported that then-Rep. Crutchfield applied for a job in Gov.-elect Stein's administration while weighing a veto override on SB 382. Unnamed sources believed a job was offered for his support of the veto. Crutchfield said he applied like hundreds of others and no offer was made. He voted to override. Stein called the claim untrue.

endorsements.text: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey he says Cabarrus County Sheriff Van Shaw endorsed him. This is the candidate's own claim; Ballotpedia did not identify any endorsements for the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We could not find a readable list of bills he sponsored in the NC House, so there is no confirmed record of his legislative actions beyond his own descriptions. He says he sponsored the HOPE Act on human trafficking, and no independent page confirms this. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land purchases, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B visas, or teacher pay. We found no pledge on outside or big-donor money. His upbringing is not documented, and the year he moved to North Carolina is not stated. The only coverage of the Stein-administration job story is a Wikipedia summary of a WBTV report, and we did not read the original report.

local.label: Roots 55: He was born in Kingston, NY and finished high school at Owego Free Academy in 1978. His campaign site describes him living in Kannapolis in 1989, and he has run a business in Concord since 1998, which points to an adult move to NC more than 25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served one term in the NC House (2023-2025), where he sat on Appropriations and Appropriations on Education. Worked at IBM for about 15 years, then co-founded and runs Casco Signs (50+ employees) and other business ventures.
qual.why: One term of legislative service plus decades of business ownership and management place him in the upper-middle to high range. He has no law or formal policy career, and board and committee seats were not counted.
qual.label: One term of legislative service plus decades of business ownership and management place him in the upper-middle to high range. He has no law or formal policy career, and board and committee seats were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey he said he supported Opportunity Scholarships (school vouchers) and wants parents to have education options.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he described himself as a pro-life supporter and listed protecting the unborn as a policy passion and campaign message.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he will defend the right to keep and bear arms and fight legislation that makes firearms harder to purchase.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he delivered funding for the Sheriff's Office and local law enforcement and supported increased pay and resources for first responders. This is his own account of his record.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

cands.name: April Cook
cands.bio: Nonprofit healthcare executive from Concord. Co-founded the Cook Community Clinic (formerly Lake Norman Community Health Clinic), a free clinic, and led it as executive director for over two decades. CEO of the NC Association of Free and Charitable Clinics since 2022. Democrat; State Senate District 34 member-elect.
cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she first came to North Carolina. Her campaign platform page was cut off at the start of its AI and Data Centers section, so her stated position on data centers is unknown. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. She has held no prior elected office, so there are no official actions to report. We found no news coverage of controversies. The only endorsements found are informal online voter-guide recommendations, which we did not treat as notable endorsements.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Co-founded a free health clinic and ran it as executive director for more than 20 years. Has been CEO of the statewide NC Association of Free and Charitable Clinics since 2022, advocating for clinics across the state. Studied business at NC State and holds an MBA from Meredith College. No prior elected office.
qual.why: Her long career as a nonprofit executive and manager fits the middle range for the role. She has no legislative service or direct budget-writing record. Board seats and chairs were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Her platform says healthcare decisions belong with women and their doctors. It pledges to protect medical decision-making from political interference and to preserve access to timely, safe healthcare, and it lists reproductive rights as an issue.
